title: EV Charger O&M Service: Scope, SLA and Spares | Anari
meta: What our operations and maintenance service covers: monitoring, preventive schedule, critical spares, escalation path and how SLA terms are set per site.

sections.h1: Operations and maintenance, defined before you sign.
sections.lede: Most O&M contracts are written after commissioning, when the site is already down and the vendor has the leverage. Ours is defined at handover: what is monitored, what is stocked on site, who is called, and how response obligations are measured.
sections.credit: Depot environment · where downtime means a cancelled service

sections.h2: Five things an O&M contract must name
sections.lede: If any of these is vague in the contract, it becomes a dispute the first time a port is down. We scope them explicitly.

items.title: Remote monitoring
items.text: Every site runs on ANARI OS: session data, fault codes and power-stage state are visible remotely, so faults are detected before a driver reports them.

items.title: Preventive schedule
items.text: Connector inspection, filter and fan cleaning, torque checks and firmware policy on a fixed cadence — with the interval set by climate and duty cycle, not by a generic annual visit.

items.title: Critical spares
items.text: At least one power module per DC cabinet type and the connector parts that cause the longest outages, held on site or in-region, so an ocean crossing is not on the critical path.

items.title: First-line and escalation
items.text: Level-1 work (resets, connector swap, cleaning, visual checks) is trained on site; cabinet-level and electrical work escalates under warranty to the responsible party, with the boundary written down.

items.title: Reporting you can audit
items.text: Uptime measured per port per month rather than as a fleet average, with outage reasons and exclusions listed — the same basis regulators use for publicly funded DC sites.

sections.h2: Five clauses that decide whether an SLA protects you
sections.lede: These are the clauses that separate a service plan from a marketing promise. We write them into the contract before the site is live.

items.title: Uptime measured per port
items.text: Per port, per month — not a fleet average that lets one dead port hide behind twenty healthy ones. We state the measurement window and the exclusions.

items.title: Downtime defined by function
items.text: A port counts as down when it cannot deliver its rated session, not only when the hardware is dead. Partial functionality is still downtime for the driver.

items.title: Response clock starts at detection
items.text: The response obligation begins when monitoring detects the fault, not when the operator calls — otherwise slow detection is free for the vendor and expensive for you.

items.title: Financial consequence
items.text: A service credit per percentage point below target. Without a consequence, the uptime target is commentary.

items.title: Independent data
items.text: Uptime figures you can audit against session records and payment logs, rather than vendor self-reporting.

items.title: What we will not promise
items.text: A blanket number for every market. Fault exposure differs by climate, grid quality and duty cycle, so targets are set per site with the basis written down.

sections.h2: What the failure modes actually are
sections.lede: The service plan is shaped by what failed on delivered sites, not by a generic checklist.

kv.v: Czechia 12-unit bus depot: a port down is a cancelled service and a passenger complaint, so the spares and escalation model is built around schedule protection.
Cambodia 240 kW site: zero weather-related downtime in the first monsoon quarter, with the customer returning for further sites.
Jordan corridor: rated output held through summer operation above 45 °C — the constraint on maintenance there is heat exposure of components, not hardware capacity.
ANARI OS monitoring and N-Tech after handover are the two layers that make detection and first response faster than a phone call to a distributor.
